reading.title: Two Questions at Lunch
reading.intro_zh: 这篇短文不复述 Mrs. Rumbold 的宴会，而是换到一个音乐营午餐：一个学生试着礼貌寒暄，用 Will you be doing...? 问未来安排，同时学会观察对方是否愿意继续聊。
passage: During a music camp lunch, Nina sat beside a quiet boy named Tom. The hostess of the camp meal asked older students to help new guests feel welcome, so Nina tried to make conversation. Tom did not even look up at first; he was busy cutting his noodles into tiny pieces. Nina smiled and asked, "Will you be joining the rehearsal this afternoon?" "No," Tom said. She tried another light question: "Will you be watching the concert tonight?" Tom shook his head and answered, "Maybe from the back." For a moment, Nina felt almost in despair, but then she noticed his tired eyes. "I see. Enjoy your lunch," she said. Tom finally smiled. Polite talk is not only asking more questions; sometimes it means talking less and letting another person rest.

questions.question: Where did Nina try to make conversation with Tom?
options: At a music camp lunch.
At a theatre called The Globe.
On a train during the holidays.
In a school office before class.
questions.explanation_zh: 短文第一句说 During a music camp lunch，Nina 坐在 Tom 旁边并试着寒暄。

questions.question: Which two polite future questions did Nina ask?
options: Whether Tom had eaten more and talked less.
Whether Tom would be joining the rehearsal and watching the concert.
Whether Tom had seen Mrs. Rumbold at dinner.
Whether Tom wanted to leave the camp at once.
questions.explanation_zh: Nina 问的是 Will you be joining the rehearsal...? 和 Will you be watching the concert...?，都是礼貌地问未来安排。

questions.question: How did Tom answer Nina's questions?
options: He gave long stories about the concert.
He asked Nina many questions in return.
He answered very briefly: "No" and "Maybe from the back."
He told the hostess to change his seat.
questions.explanation_zh: Tom 的回答很短，一个是 No，另一个是 Maybe from the back，说明他不太想展开聊天。

questions.question: What did Nina finally realize?
options: Tom was tired and did not really want a long conversation.
Tom wanted her to ask five more questions.
The hostess had made a mistake about lunch.
The rehearsal had already finished.
questions.explanation_zh: Nina noticed his tired eyes，所以她明白 Tom 可能只是累了，不想继续长时间聊天。

questions.question: What social lesson does the story teach?
options: A polite person should never speak at lunch.
Short answers always mean someone is rude.
If one topic fails, we must keep asking harder questions.
Polite talk means asking gently, reading signals, and stopping gracefully.
questions.explanation_zh: 结尾点出 Polite talk is not only asking more questions，有时也要 talking less，让别人休息。

writing.intro_zh: 今天抓五个 Lesson 40 的餐桌寒暄句式：用 asked...to...写安排，用 did not even...写没有回应，用 was busy doing...写正忙于某事，用 Will you be...?礼貌询问未来安排，再用 if you...more and...less 写带反差的建议。

patterns.title: asked ... to ...
patterns.source: The hostess asked me to sit next to Mrs. Rumbold.
patterns.focus_zh: asked...to... 用来写一个人请、要求或安排另一个人做某事。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写老师、主人、队长或朋友请某人坐下、帮忙、加入活动或照顾新同学。
patterns.sample: The teacher asked me to sit next to a new student at lunch.
patterns.tip_zh: asked 后面先接人，再用 to 加动词原形：asked me to sit, asked us to help。

patterns.title: did not even ...
patterns.source: She did not even look up when I took my seat beside her.
patterns.focus_zh: did not even... 强调连一个很小的反应都没有，能写出尴尬或冷淡的场面。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人忙着吃饭、看书或休息，连抬头、回答或微笑都没有。
patterns.sample: He did not even look up when I said hello at the table.
patterns.tip_zh: did not even 后面接动词原形，比如 look, answer, smile。

patterns.title: was busy doing ...
patterns.source: In a short time, she was busy eating.
patterns.focus_zh: was busy doing... 写某人正忙着做一件事，注意 busy 后面接 doing。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写某人在午餐、活动或课间正忙着吃饭、准备节目、收拾东西或看菜单。
patterns.sample: My partner was busy reading the menu and did not hear me.
patterns.tip_zh: busy 后面通常接动名词：busy eating, busy reading, busy preparing。

patterns.title: Will you be doing ...?
patterns.source: Will you be spending your holidays abroad this year?
patterns.focus_zh: Will you be doing...? 不是硬问“你做不做”，而是轻轻问“到时候你是不是会有这个安排”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：用 Will you be...? 礼貌地问别人明天、周末、假期或活动期间的安排。
patterns.sample: Will you be joining the school dinner tomorrow evening?
patterns.tip_zh: Will you be 后面接 doing 形式，比如 joining, watching, staying, spending。

patterns.title: if you ... more and ... less
patterns.source: If you ate more and talked less, we would both enjoy our dinner.
patterns.focus_zh: if you...more and...less 用 more / less 做对比，可以写出一句带反差的建议或幽默收束。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：写如果某人多做一件有帮助的事、少做一件打扰人的事，结果会更好。
patterns.sample: If you listened more and worried less, the meeting would feel easier.
patterns.tip_zh: more 和 less 前面各放一个动作或状态，形成清楚对比：listen more, talk less。
